content.text: Where is the threshold computed, and which files use it?
Two different questions. "Where is it computed" is a concept, so `search_code` (semantic when an index is ready); the callers are a literal token, which is `grep`'s job.

content.name: search_code
content.text:
[semantic index]
pkg/sizes.py:1  threshold  def threshold(n):
  FILE -- use this exact path with view_file/replace_text
pkg/budget.py:12  spend  cap = threshold(total)
  FILE -- use this exact path with view_file/replace_text
The definition is pkg/sizes.py:1. For every call site, grep the literal `threshold(` with `regex=False`; as a regex the parenthesis would open a group.

content.name: grep
content.text:
3 match(es)
pkg/sizes.py:1: def threshold(n):
pkg/budget.py:12:     cap = threshold(total)
tests/test_sizes.py:4:     assert threshold(10) == 5
One definition, two callers. A listing of pkg shows whether any module there was missed.

`threshold` is computed in pkg/sizes.py:1 (`def threshold(n)`). It is used in pkg/budget.py:12 (`cap = threshold(total)`) and tests/test_sizes.py:4. Each tool did one job: `search_code` found the concept without knowing the exact name, `grep` with `regex=False` listed every literal call site, and `ls` confirmed pkg holds only those modules, so nothing was missed.
